entry.title: Kissonerga Beach, Paphos
entry.summary: Kissonerga Beach is a quiet stretch of pebbles and rock on the coast north of Paphos, below the village of Kissonerga. The water is clear and the mood is relaxed, with a few tavernas and beach bars close to the shore.

entry.title: Faros Beach, Pervolia
entry.summary: Faros Beach is a quiet local sandy beach near the village of Pervolia on the coast south-west of Larnaca. It has fewer hotels and crowds than the main Larnaca beaches and is popular with local families at weekends.

entry.title: Kefalos Beach, Paphos
entry.summary: Kefalos Beach is a sandy beach near the Paphos lighthouse on the west edge of Kato Paphos. It is usually quieter than the harbour area, with calm, shallow water and a view of the lighthouse at the point.

entry.title: Venus Beach, Paphos
entry.summary: Venus Beach is a sandy beach on the coastal road north of Kato Paphos, close to the Tombs of the Kings. It is named for Aphrodite, the goddess said to have been born on this coast. Hotels line the road behind the beach and the water is shallow and calm.

entry.title: Alykes Beach, Kato Paphos
entry.summary: Alykes Beach is a small town beach in Kato Paphos, close to the harbour, the castle and the archaeological sites. It works well for a short swim between sightseeing stops, with cafes and restaurants within easy walking distance.

entry.title: Mackenzie Beach, Larnaca
entry.summary: Mackenzie Beach is a sandy beach just south of Larnaca with a row of bars and tavernas along the sand. It lies close to the airport, so planes pass low overhead on landing, which is part of the attraction for plane spotters. The water is shallow and warm.

entry.title: Lara Beach, Akamas
entry.summary: Lara Beach is a sandy bay on the wild west coast of the Akamas peninsula, one of the places where green and loggerhead turtles nest in summer. Access is by a rough track from the Agios Georgios side, which keeps the bay quiet and the surroundings unspoilt.

entry.title: Sunrise Beach, Protaras
entry.summary: Sunrise Beach is a sandy beach on the Protaras coast with calm, shallow water and a line of hotels behind it. It is a convenient family beach with services close by, and it faces east, so the morning light is good.

entry.title: Ayia Thekla Beach
entry.summary: Ayia Thekla Beach lies on the coast west of Ayia Napa beside a small seaside chapel. The sand is soft, the water is calm and shallow, and the beach is quieter than the main resort beaches, which makes it popular with local families.

entry.title: Landa Beach, Ayia Napa
entry.summary: Landa Beach is a golden sand beach a short walk west of Nissi Beach in Ayia Napa, with shallow, clear water and a calmer feel than its busier neighbour. It suits families and anyone who wants Ayia Napa sand without the crowds of Nissi.

entry.title: Finikoudes Beach, Larnaca
entry.summary: Finikoudes is a sandy city beach with a palm-lined promenade in the centre of Larnaca, with shallow water and cafes just behind the sand. It is lively in the evening and convenient for visitors without a car.

entry.title: Latchi Beach, Polis
entry.summary: Latchi, or Latsi, is a small fishing harbour near Polis with a pebble and coarse sand beach and a line of seafront tavernas serving fresh fish. It is a quiet base for the Akamas peninsula and boat trips along the coast.

entry.title: Pissouri Bay Beach
entry.summary: Pissouri Bay Beach is a long beach of pebbles and coarse sand on the south coast between Limassol and Paphos, with a quieter feel than the larger resorts. White cliffs frame the bay and the village sits on the hill above.

entry.title: Governor's Beach, Limassol
entry.summary: Governor's Beach lies below white chalk cliffs between Limassol and Larnaca, with dark grey sand and pebbles that contrast with the pale rock. The water is clear and the beach has a mix of organised areas and quieter stretches.

entry.title: Petra tou Romiou (Aphrodite's Rock)
entry.summary: Petra tou Romiou, also called Aphrodite's Rock, is a pebble beach with sea stacks that legend links to the birth of Aphrodite. It is a famous stop on the road between Limassol and Paphos, and the sea can be rough, so many visitors come for the view and a short dip.

entry.title: Coral Bay, Peyia
entry.summary: Coral Bay near Peyia is a sandy bay sheltered between two headlands, with calm, shallow water and a well-developed resort strip behind it. It is one of the most popular beaches in the Paphos area for families.

entry.title: Konnos Bay, Cape Greco
entry.summary: Konnos Bay is a small sandy cove at the foot of pine-covered cliffs near Cape Greco, with clear turquoise water that is good for snorkelling. A short walk leads to the headlands of the Cape Greco national forest park.

entry.title: Fig Tree Bay, Protaras
entry.summary: Fig Tree Bay is a sheltered sandy bay in Protaras with shallow, calm water that suits children and beginners. A small rocky outcrop with a fig tree gives the bay its name, and cafes line the promenade behind the beach.

entry.title: Makronissos Beach, Ayia Napa
entry.summary: Makronissos Beach is a long sandy beach on the east side of Ayia Napa with calm, shallow water and a more relaxed feel than Nissi Beach. Ancient rock-cut tombs lie close to the beach and can be visited on the same trip.

entry.title: Nissi Beach, Ayia Napa
entry.summary: Nissi Beach is a wide white-sand beach on the edge of Ayia Napa, with shallow turquoise water and a small islet that can be reached by wading in calm weather. It is one of the liveliest beaches in Cyprus, with beach bars, music and watersports in summer.

entry.title: Port de Pollenca Beach
entry.summary: The beach at Port de Pollenca runs along the sheltered Bay of Pollenca in northern Mallorca, with a promenade and the pine-lined Passeig Anglada Camarasa behind it. The sand is fine and the water is calm and shallow near the shore, which suits families and swimmers. Cafes, restaurants and small shops are a few steps from the sand.

entry.title: Kourouta Beach
entry.summary: Kourouta is a long, wide sandy beach on the Ionian coast of Elis in the western Peloponnese, a short drive from Amaliada. The shore is flat and the water stays shallow for some distance, with beach bars and tavernas just behind the sand. It is a laid-back local beach rather than an international resort, and afternoon breezes are common on this open stretch of coast.

entry.title: Es Caragol Beach
entry.summary: Es Caragol is a quiet natural beach near Colonia de Sant Jordi on the south coast of Mallorca. Fine pale sand slopes gently into shallow, clear turquoise water, which keeps the sea calm and easy for children. Compared with the resort beaches nearby it has little development behind the sand, so it feels open and relaxed, and the sea is usually warmest from July to September.

entry.title: anj Beach, Bar
entry.summary: anj is a small resort on the coast of Bar Municipality in southern Montenegro. The beach is about 1 km long and mostly sand mixed with some pebbles, and its main stretch is known as Biserna Obala (the Pearl Coast). Hotels, cottages, bars and restaurants line the shore and are busiest in summer, and there are showers and toilets nearby.

entry.title: Velika Plaa, Ulcinj
entry.summary: Velika Plaa (Big Beach) is a sandy strip of roughly 12 km (sources give 12 to 14 km) that runs from Ulcinj south to the Bojana river near Ada Bojana. The water stays shallow for a long way out, and steady afternoon winds make it one of the leading kitesurfing spots in the Balkans, with several schools at the southern end. Dunes and a protected natural area sit behind the sand, with beach bars and restaurants at intervals.

entry.title: Plage de Palavas-les-Flots
entry.summary: Palavas-les-Flots is a seaside town near Montpellier with a wide sandy beach, a promenade and a lighthouse by the canal. The water is shallow and warm in summer. It is easy to reach by tram and bus from Montpellier.

entry.title: Plage de Granville
entry.summary: Granville is a seaside town in Normandy with a sandy beach below its old town on the cliff. The tide here is among the biggest in Europe, so the beach changes dramatically through the day. The water is cool and swimming is best at high tide.

entry.title: Utah Beach, Normandy
entry.summary: Utah Beach is a wide, flat beach on the east coast of the Cotentin peninsula in Normandy, one of the D-Day landing beaches. The sand stretches far at low tide and memorials and a museum stand behind the dunes. The sea is Atlantic and swimming is possible in calm weather.

entry.title: Plage de la Conche des Baleines, Ile de Re
entry.summary: La Conche des Baleines is a wide sandy beach on the north-west tip of Ile de Re, with dunes and the Phare des Baleines lighthouse nearby. It is exposed to Atlantic waves and best for walking and cycling. Swimming depends on the tide and the sea state.

entry.title: Plage de la Palmyre
entry.summary: La Palmyre is a wide sandy beach on the Atlantic coast of Charente-Maritime, beside the Foret de la Coubre. The sea is Atlantic, so it is cooler than the Mediterranean. The resort has a promenade, a zoo nearby and cycle paths through the pines.
